capabilities: Syncs inline tables two-way with CSV files
Writes self-updating inline tables of contents
Lists notes by tag or folder
Draws charts from CSV, TSV, JSON or YAML files
Builds custom components in Ruby, JavaScript or Markdown
extras: Warns that bare syntax can overwrite content beneath directives like list:; JavaScript components run sandboxed inside the plugin with no Node APIs; main.js is about 8.5 MB because it bundles Ruby compiled to WebAssembly.
problem: Generated content like tables of contents, note lists and charts goes stale because Obsidian has no built-in way to keep it in sync with the notes and data files it comes from.
summary: Markdown superset that generates inline tables, TOCs, lists and charts from directives and syncs tables with CSV files.
